title: An irreducible multiway system cannot be both complete and consistent

fields.label: Label
fields.value: An irreducible multiway system cannot be both complete and consistent

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: If questions about the long-run evolution of a multiway system (an idealized axiom system) are undecidable, then the system cannot be both complete and consistent, because completeness plus consistency would give a procedure that always terminates to decide whether a string is reached.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: So the result of this is that if the evolution of a multiway system is computationally irreducible—so that questions about its ultimate behavior are undecidable—the system cannot be both complete and consistent.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Implications for Mathematics and Its Foundations” (from p. 772), p. 783. Scope: multiway systems interpreted as axiom systems with a negation operation

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-31: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.85

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Under explicit effectiveness assumptions, this is a standard proof-level implication and can be formally checked now. Its validity hinges on distinguishing irreducibility from undecidability, but that ambiguity can be exposed rather than requiring new observations.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Formalize reachability, negation, consistency, completeness, and effective enumeration for the multiway axiom system. Prove that complete consistency supplies a terminating parallel search for each statement or its negation, contradicting undecidability, or provide a countermodel violating an assumption.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The result requires effective negation and enumeration assumptions.

Computational irreducibility alone does not imply undecidability.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The sentence is a conditional theorem, and the proof is the standard one: completeness plus consistency is itself a decision procedure for the string-or-negation question. It matches formalized incompleteness arguments and can be checked directly for multiway systems with a negation operation. Within the stated scope, existing proof methods resolve it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Assume reachability of an arbitrary string is undecidable and negation is computable. Completeness plus consistency would decide reachability by searching until the string or its negation appears. Deriving that contradiction confirms the implication; exhibiting a complete consistent system with undecidable reachability would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Irreducibility enters only by supplying undecidability of reachability, which is the actual hypothesis.

The argument assumes finitely specified rules and a computable negation.
